purpose: Source-change review guard, not a refinement proof. See formal/README.md.

EOA Uncertain retains exact borrowed wire on all dispatch errors; same-identity retry stutters in EoaRecovery, included receipt only restores submitted projection. NOOP reserves submitted hash before dispatch; automatic NOOP reconciliation is not modeled or implemented.

Exact attempt and unchanged checkpoint no-ops retain health/owner/CAS guards; admission overload makes no durable transition. Retained terminal retries do not enqueue new work.
Solana independent signature reservation precedes Redis attempt storage; missing projection after SQL commit parks. The Redis and authority models are separate and not mechanically composed.

Bundled EIP-7702 is disabled and legacy work parks; no dedicated protocol qualification is claimed. Streaming export, HTTP authentication/semaphores and provider genesis checks are outside the state-machine proof.

progress_scheduling_followup.reason: Reviewed successful-cycle result construction: sent counts only moved-to-submitted acknowledgments, recovered counts submitted-projection reconciliation/acknowledgment, while uncertain attempts retain borrowed state. depth_checkpoint_followup.status: Source correspondence reviewed and formatted candidate fingerprints recorded; implementation and TLC execution pending.
depth_checkpoint_followup.reason: The former Finality abstraction collapses heights and cannot detect persisting the observed tip above the probabilistic depth-qualified boundary. DepthCheckpoint now separates H, Q=H-depth, persisted anchor, independent canonical history and semantic qualified witness; tip-anchor and ignored-conflict mutations exercise distinct failures. Core and real-journal executor regressions retain within-assessment tip revalidation, allow shallow tip replacement, halt on qualified-boundary conflict, and preserve finalized/legacy conservative behavior. Monotonic journal CAS, multiple advancing checkpoints and composition remain outside this new single-checkpoint model.

capacity_scheduling_followup.status: One-line bounded scheduling experiment reviewed and candidate fingerprint recorded; implementation and measurement pending.

capacity_polling_health_followup.status: Formatted candidate source reviewed; validation pending.
capacity_polling_health_followup.reason: Whole-second Solana polling configuration 1..5 defaults to the prior effective one-second queue delay. Only accepted-send/provisional-status/throttled observation scheduling changes; wire/signature, finalized evidence and lifetime send/read counters retain their transitions. capacity_polling_health_followup.test_compile_repair: The new Solana regression uses let-Ok-else instead of unwrap because its existing JobError intentionally lacks Debug; only failure diagnostics changed, no runtime transition.

gap_recovery_followup.status: Source reviewed after formatting and passing implementation suites; full model rerun recorded separately.
gap_recovery_followup.reason: The bounded getter reads an existing EOA attempt and rejects mismatched key/kind, terminal/quarantined admission or halted chain; it is not dispatch authorization. Replay decodes/re-encodes original EIP-2718 bytes, checks nonce/hash/sender/chain/attempt membership, rechecks owner and runs before_eoa again. No signing, fee change, replay-key mutation or terminal proof is added. Repeated original transmission collapses to stuttering in EoaRecovery/DisasterRecovery; sent is possible future delivery, not an evictable mempool. Retained cached consumed-count high-water supports the allocator floor, but NonceAllocator assumes monotonic chain consumption and does not model actual rollback. Fixed recovery windows, owner-fenced cooldown reservations, 32 sequential calls, missing-gap stop, actual counter progress and unchanged unknown-response behavior are implementation regression obligations, not newly proved scheduling/liveness properties. The 11-scenario real Redis/HTTP/SQLite parent test and broad executor/core suites passed; process reorg qualification remains separate. NOOP gaps and missing authoritative/projection data can stay unresolved.

reorg_oracle_followup.status: Source and existing passing implementation evidence reviewed; model rerun pending and not claimed by this metadata correction.
reorg_oracle_followup.reason: The strict process oracle now separates a retained attempt from transmissions: one unchanged durable wire must have an additional accepted Engine-only proxy send after the fault, then match the independently fetched signed transaction, canonical receipt/block, reserved nonce, outcome and delayed terminal proof. Terminal admission replay must add no send or attempt. The explicit legacy comparison option alone accepts an execution-equivalent fee replacement. Seven offline unittest methods include positive witnesses and adversarial evidence substitutions; their synthetic signatures do not verify cryptography. Normal and reverted real Anvil process cases passed against unchanged runtime binary a3d360eba3dc470bd830ec9d3a32e0be8e11b6764f9bbf6efeb319f080eb8515. Finality covers provisional versus terminal observations; EoaRecovery/DisasterRecovery cover retained identity and durable membership. Repeated identical dispatch is a stutter in the identity abstractions, not a new protocol transition. No model changes or new TLC cases are justified by this test-only oracle correction. Actual mempool eviction, timing, request pacing, node encoding and implementation/model composition remain outside those proofs. The capacity_faults.py mapping guards the shared raw-wire encoding and Engine-only accepted-send counter dependency; it does not claim formal coverage of the full capacity harness.

history_index_followup.status: Actual applied source matches independently reviewed draft; targeted implementation suites passed without source repairs; full model rerun recorded separately.
history_index_followup.reason: Nonunique (id,sequence) indexes change only physical lookup structure. Existing SQL ordering, every logical row/replay binding/checkpoint/Redis marker, and schema version remain unchanged. Initialization includes both in its existing transaction; writable open uses owner/health-fenced one-transaction DDL then rechecks health before returning a handle. Read-only/offline operations do not migrate. The owned startup task and blocking closure each retain the journal Arc through cancellation. Five real journal tests passed: populated legacy restart/export/token equality and query plans; first/latest membership and contradictory proof retention; readonly/owner/health gates; second-statement DDL rollback; deterministic caller and async-startup cancellation while an independent WAL writer blocks DDL. The migration stutters over DisasterRecovery logical state; SQLite DDL atomicity, real power loss, OS locks and Tokio cancellation remain implementation assumptions/tests, not new model theorems. No lookup-throughput improvement or bound on retained/per-ID history is claimed.

broadcast_concurrency_followup.status: Applied formatted source matches reviewed draft; workspace compilation and existing targeted suites passed; measured higher-setting qualification remains separate.
broadcast_concurrency_followup.reason: Actual QueueConfig accepts integer/environment-text broadcast concurrency1..128 with default32, wired through manager/handler/worker. Only existing new/recycled/borrowed ordered send buffers are configured; normal preparation stays32, NOOP combined prepare/send uses min(setting,32), borrowed receipt reads have a local32 permit cap released before send, gap replay and fee bumps stay sequential. Layered EngineConfig tests verify omitted/default/numeric/text/range/type handling; fixture additions retain32. Nonce windows, batch reservation, signed wire, journal preauthorization, ordered result attribution and unknown-response handling retain their prior transitions. Nondeterministic authorized dispatch was already modeled; no new TLA case or count is warranted. The models do not verify futures/Tokio scheduling, actual global/per-worker concurrency, RPC rates, wall-clock fairness, lease-loss overlap, or capacity. This is an experimental per-worker setting, not evidence of a throughput gain.

diagnostic_retention_followup.status: Applied formatted source independently reviewed; isolated eight-test Redis/serializer suite passed and both no-trim negative controls failed as intended. Full finite-model rerun recorded separately.
diagnostic_retention_followup.reason: All six single/multilane nack, failure and deserialization-failure append sites retain the same owner-fenced completion boundary and add newest-first LTRIM100. Metadata attempts, retry/backoff inputs, queue order/delay, lease state, hook pipeline, dedupe, cancellation and expiry operations do not change. Whole-tree reader review found no retry/protocol decision based on diagnostic cardinality; Solana orphan detection observes key existence, preserved by oversized-record omission markers. Bounded serialization preserves ordinary JobErrorRecord JSON, emits a distinct valid omission envelope above16KiB and preserves unrelated Serialize errors. Diagnostic inspection/size/order are outside QueueLease protocol variables, so these writes project to the same existing completion action (or stutter over diagnostic-only state); no new theorem or model/configuration is added. The model still assumes valid Redis key types and successful EXEC commands: Redis command errors may partially execute, and this patch does not strengthen that excluded failure boundary. Serializer byte bounds, TTL behavior, stale-owner append/trim rejection, attempt increments and legacy trim/turnover costs are implementation checks, not TLC proofs. External typed inspectors must recognize omission envelopes; legacy oversized entries age out, first large trim can be linear, and total/global retention remains outside the per-job cap.

dispatch_pipeline_followup.status: Final owned-Arc source reviewed after four intended negative-control failures, restored seven-send-test pass and formatting check. Full finite-model rerun recorded separately; previous evidence preserved.
dispatch_pipeline_followup.reason: Both new/recycled production paths first reserve signed borrowed wires as a batch, then authorize each wire in input order through immutable admission/wire validation and independent journal commit/mirror. Redis worker ownership is read on both sides of awaited authorization. One authorized network wait can overlap the next authorization; ordered bounded results retain ID association. First authorization error stops the producer; shared first-poll failure flag suppresses buffered unstarted sends, while already-started calls drain before returning that error. Entire batch remains borrowed on authorization error/cancellation; RPC errors remain Uncertain rather than terminal/recyclable. EoaRecovery already permits independent retained-identity Broadcast; DisasterRecovery permits authorized Send during later AttemptCommit/Mirror and late execution after halt/crash. Suppressed send is conservative non-delivery, not a new safety transition. Models do not represent whole-batch barriers, first-poll revocation, Tokio buffers/Arc/atomics, worker-owner reads, ordered responses, cancellation/draining mechanics, recycled preparation, concurrency/rate/fairness or throughput; no new theorem/configuration/refinement proof is claimed. Six new real Redis/SQLite/HTTP regressions verify these implementation cuts, including both actual entry points and real higher nonce4 around holes2/3. Four runtime mutations (whole-batch barrier, missing producer stop, missing post-owner fence, missing first-poll suppression) fail intended assertions/deadlines; compilation succeeds. A prior fixture with recycled nonces above highest submitted1 was correctly rejected by cleanup and repaired, not accepted as a runtime bug.

pr_review_oct11.status: Source transitions reviewed; executable checks recorded separately. This fingerprint is a review guard, not a proof of Rust refinement.
pr_review_oct11.reason: Journal mutations retain their owned task, serial lock and admission slot from health check through SQLite commit, Redis CAS and postcheck. Blocking DB closures separately retain the file owner. Caller cancellation grants no permission and performs no chain send; OS/runtime crash still exposes the old fail-closed checkpoint gap. DisasterRecovery now models unavailable observation as a distinct halt that offline reattach may clear only with the exact authority token; primary role remains a runtime obligation. Other halt causes and chain/terminal conflicts stay non-clearable. Solana serialized admission/preflight uses processed while status/receipt evidence remains finalized; a missing pre-sign hash retries with unchanged serialized input, and simulation errors never imply global non-execution. Existing identity models abstract this admission filter and same-wire retries; parked attempts issue nonterminal NACK notifications through the owner-fenced completion pipeline without releasing identity. Supplied-gas EVM estimation filters invalid envelopes before signing without altering gas; intentional execution reverts remain valid. Redis pool reconnect only precedes WATCH and never retries EXEC. SIGTERM enters existing shutdown; webhook admission policy/read-only route exceptions do not authorize mutation. Concrete task lifetimes, signals, webhooks, node fee/gas/capability policies, JSON numeric precision, redaction, connection timings, and throughput remain implementation tests/review obligations, not model theorems. Final shutdown review adds a read-guard registration before spawning each mutation and an explicit write-barrier drain after all HTTP/workers finish; a regression covers unpolled registration and canceled commit-to-mirror work. This prevents orderly runtime shutdown from aborting detached publication, without changing forced-crash model transitions.

queue_shutdown_oct12.status: Source cancellation boundaries reviewed; executable validation is recorded separately. No model action or configuration changed.
queue_shutdown_oct12.reason: Single and multilane worker loops prioritize shutdown and observe it while awaiting Redis pop or error backoff. Cancellation before Lua applies stutters over QueueLease; an applied pop with an unseen reply maps to Poll then stuttering, retaining its lease until Expire and a later Poll. Shutdown does not create a completion, dispatch the unseen job, or cancel active handlers or their lease-fenced completion. WATCH/EXISTS/EXEC and journal ownership/drain are unchanged. Real-Redis tests withhold applied pop replies in both queue types, require bounded shutdown, then reclaim the original job through explicit lease expiry and observe one successful hook. A separate gated handler checks active work still drains through acknowledgement. Redis reconnect timing, response loss, Tokio cancellation, wall-clock shutdown bounds and liveness remain implementation obligations, not finite-model theorems. The active-job log count correction is diagnostic only.

health_capacity_fairness_oct12.reason: Health checks acquire their bounded chain lane cancellably before reserving one of32 global health slots. Only after both permits are held does run_owned register and spawn. The owned operation consumes that same lane in serial_guard_with_lane, retaining both permits through any pending checkpoint repair, FULL acknowledgement and final observation. Cancellation before registration grants no permission and releases acquired permits; after registration the existing drain barrier retains work. Authority transactions, Redis CAS, acknowledgement, finality and send gates are unchanged, so protocol actions are unchanged. Real Redis tests reject hot-chain slot monopolization, bound detached operations across distinct lanes, and check cancellation/drain at both admission boundaries. FIFO ordering, Tokio scheduling and performance remain implementation obligations, not a new finite-model liveness proof.

retained_recovery_oct12.status: Runtime, tests and model correspondence reviewed independently. Executable validation is recorded separately; hashes are source-change guards, not refinement proofs.
retained_recovery_oct12.reason: Schema3 retains recovery mode and cumulative grant count/time in the independent authority. A missing Redis Solana attempt is restored only from a unique canonical retained row after immutable admission, digest, binding, cryptographic wire, blockhash and fee-payer checks; storage-token SET NX never overwrites conflicting data. Restoration grants no send permission. Recovered sends consume a FULL-committed grant through the existing pending-token publication/acknowledgement protocol and recheck Redis ownership before dispatch; cancellation and lost replies burn grants. Durable mode rejects ordinary authorization despite a rolled-back Redis flag. Only the extra20 grants are independently bounded; the conditional20+20 model assumes the original Redis counter is retained before mode activation, and a named boundary shows that assumption failing. The Redis-only Solana model retains its loss boundary; the new retained model and projection model are separate abstractions with no composition theorem. Offline reattach accepts only a primary observation of the exact target, atomically acknowledges pending state and adopts the process identity, then reobserves. Predecessor/missing/foreign markers, unrelated halts and authority loss remain fail-closed. Schema1/2 upgrade, historical schema2 pending repair, serialization, SQL/Redis error behavior, cryptography, filesystem durability, polling costs, wall-clock spacing and throughput require implementation checks. Historical missing-projection-parks notes describe earlier behavior and are superseded only by this supported exact-record restoration path. The existing CI harness invocation now runs retained-Redis and missing-projection scenarios in separate disposable fixtures by default; explicit flags select one case. Reports stay separate and no workflow permission change is needed.

recovery_readability_followup.status: Behavior-preserving source correspondence reviewed; execution evidence is recorded separately.
recovery_readability_followup.reason: The five offline administration methods move verbatim into operations.rs, preserving owner-lock and transaction scopes, all ten awaits, exact-target acknowledgement/adoption and fresh post-observation. Solana execute_transaction retains admission, storage and journal-binding gates, then directly awaits either retained-attempt reconciliation or initial build/sign/persist/send. Extracted bodies preserve operation order, finality-before-expiry and the second history observation after expiry. No task, permission, new signature path, RPC, grant, schema or durability policy is introduced. Models and bounds remain unchanged; source hashes are a change-review guard, not a refinement proof. Existing crash/cancellation/recovery tests and matched load remain the executable regression checks.

eoa_envelope_review_nov08.reason: Preparation explicitly selects CREATE or CALL, preserves legacy estimation, and rejects out-of-range gas rather than overflowing. Durable replay keys, broadcast authorization, fee-bump arithmetic and finality are unchanged. Existing models and bounds are unchanged; they do not prove Alloy construction or RPC gas arithmetic. Executable regressions cover signed CREATE identity and hostile estimates. The local Engine/Redis/Anvil harness checks deployed runtime, predicted addresses, value, crash recovery and duplicate retries.

durable_cancellation_nov08.reason: Cancellation checks unsigned status and moves the intent to existing quarantined state in one FULL authority transaction before queue mutation. It shares serialization with before_broadcast; existing replay/attempt evidence prevents cancellation. The owned task retains publication through caller cancellation. No schema, counter, retained-wire or finality-policy changes. Payload validation reuses one admitted-record snapshot instead of two reads; broadcast still revalidates current authority. IntentCancellation checks this new linearization protocol and its old cached-read counterexample; it is not a refinement or composition proof. Existing crash/rollback/source guards and executable tests remain required.

bounded_api_batches_nov08.reason: A shared preflight rejects batches above 100 items before dependency or admission effects. Five signing/ABI preparation paths use ordered Futures buffering capped at 16 in place of join_all. No tasks, signing changes, retry policy, journal identity, dispatch or finality transitions are added. Existing models and bounds are unchanged; per-request size/concurrency/order are executable HTTP and controlled-future obligations, not TLA claims.

native_environment_signer_nov08.reason: Environment-key derivation and local signing select Alloy native secp256k1 rather than k256 secret arithmetic. The development-only credential keeps its existing type and converts before signing, preserving configured chain ID. Public address validation, immutable admission, signed-wire reservation, queue serialization, nonce/finality and recovery authority are unchanged. EIP-155 fixed-wire and signature compatibility checks plus actual HTTP/Anvil process tests establish executable correspondence. The existing models/bounds are unchanged and abstract signing; hashes are a review guard, not a cryptographic, timing or Rust refinement proof. The transitive crypto-bigint advisory remains visible. Prehashes at/above the curve order may produce different valid signature bytes due to nonce preprocessing; curve-order boundary tests verify identity rather than universal byte equality. The upgrade harness starts the old binary and restarts the new one with the same state, requiring original mined transaction hashes and no duplicate effects.

solana_processing_queue_lease_nov08.reason: Queue pop attaches immutable lease key/token identity to BorrowedJob for regular and multilane queues. New Solana processing locks record that identity plus a distinct processing token. Atomic acquisition requires the current queue token and its expiring key; a known prior record may be replaced only after its queue owner is no longer live. Attempt reads/writes and final pre-RPC lock checks require both processing ownership and queue liveness, strengthening stale-worker refusal. Legacy UUID/opaque records retain conservative TTL behavior. Signed wire, admission, journal publication, grant budgets and finality/expiry policy are unchanged. Standard ERR lock-lost replies fix Redis error classification. SolanaProcessingLease abstracts the new-format conjunction of metadata and live lease key; positive invariants, two faults and an early-reclaim witness are checked. JSON/key construction, expiry timing, old-format compatibility and actual crash behavior remain executable obligations; no refinement/composition or wall-clock liveness proof is claimed.

offline_queue_reconstruction.decision: Add QueueRebuild finite model and preserve existing independent authority/retained-wire protocols.
offline_queue_reconstruction.reason: Offline CLI holds the exclusive journal owner, verifies continuity before/after bounded inventory/projection repair, starts no workers/HTTP and never grants a send. Inventory excludes terminal/quarantine and validates canonical attempt digests/replay binding. EOA repair validates all retained wire identities, preserves the nonce floor and mutates only under the current EOA owner token; unsupported/contradictory records fail closed. Solana workers still activate retained-wire recovery and consume its permanent journal budget. Existing queue counters/order/delay survive, live leases and cancellation/terminal witnesses reject repair. A new QueueRebuild model has one positive, six fault counterexamples and a successful-repair witness; file locks, numeric/encoding bounds, Redis runtime type safety, cryptography and cross-model composition remain assumptions/implementation tests. Tagged encoding only extends previously broken colon-containing EOA IDs; ordinary and supported legacy members retain their representation.

submitted_id_encoding.decision: Preserve ordinary/legacy members; tag and hex-encode IDs containing colon.
submitted_id_encoding.reason: The submitted index previously silently omitted these accepted IDs. The encoding maps to the same ID/hash/nonce model values; normal and supported legacy strings remain byte-identical. Canonical decoding is required for exact cleanup. Round-trip tests cover colon/Unicode IDs, legacy rows, malformed/noncanonical hex and cleanup identity. No claim of parsing ambiguous malformed historical colon members.
